Macrons

Consonantal i

Tools, fasteners & household repair

drill noun

also boring tool, auger, gimlet, drill bit

classical

terēbra / terebra, -ae f.

noun, first declension

boring tool, auger or gimlet

The ancient boring tool, and the natural inherited word for a modern drill. Lewis & Short marks the second vowel as variable (tĕrē̆bra). Both forms are therefore shown rather than silently choosing one reconstruction; the example Terēbram affer adopts the long-vowel variant.

Examples

  • Terēbram affer.

    Bring the drill.composed

Other words

  • perforāculum

    also used · late Latin · M-O s.v. drill

    Morgan–Owens also records perforāculum and furfuraculum; for ordinary speech we prefer the historically established terebra.

  • furfuraculum

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. drill

See also electric drill, adze.

SourcesLewis & Short: terebra · Morgan–Owens: drill

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
